Although the strength of glass fibers is lower than carbon fiber on a constituent level, the resistance to tensile side cracking is influenced by the longer glass fiber network. In case of carbon fiber in the rCF, these are produced from pyrolyzed carbon fiber and the fiber length is typically in the 0.039”-0.39” (1-10 mm) range. Hence it is hypothesized that microcracking is readily initiated in the carbon fiber on the tension side. The multiple charge layers SMC (thicker) had lower flexural strength values than single charge SMC. This suggests the three-dimensional fiber network and layer interactions in the thicker SMC reduces the in-plane fiber distribution and flexural strength. More microscopy may have to be conducted to quantify the extent of 3D movement, but the compliance of the fiber stack is hypothesized to enable such mechanism. 50 The flexural modulus of the commercial product was slightly higher attributed to consolidation pressures of 1200 psi or greater, most of the panels in our study were at ~1000 psi. Although we generally know the chemical formulation of the commercial SMC, there are several formulation specific information details that are not disclosed by the manufacturer. When we exceeded 1,000 psi, there was significant fiber wash necessitating a dedicated tool for making SMC plates at higher pressures. This was not possible within the scope of this study. TCF over molded SMC – another hybrid configuration In these studies, a continuous layer of TCF was over-molded with glass SMC on top of the TCF. This was a different variation from the hybrid SMC discussed in the earlier section. There was no precedence of studies using continuous TCF, the interface compatibility, and whether the TCF had to be pre-heated to receive the SMC etc. These were systematically addressed in this study.
